findings.issue: R6 hedge-modality: 'can carry asbestos' uses the banned hedge 'can' in a declarative. The committed Verona sibling phrases the equivalent asbestos fact indicatively ('frequently contain asbestos fibers'). The automated Rule-6 gate grep does not catch 'can', so this passes the build, but the ruleset Section 3 BANNED list bans 'can' as a hedge. Borderline/defensible because asbestos presence genuinely varies by product and era, so the cautious wording is factually honest.
findings.evidence: "...because modified bitumen and built-up roofing installed before the mid-1980s **can carry** asbestos in the felts or adhesives."
findings.fix: before: '...installed before the mid-1980s can carry asbestos in the felts or adhesives.' → after: '...installed before the mid-1980s commonly contain asbestos in the felts or adhesives.' (mirror the Verona gold 'frequently contain' indicative form).

findings.issue: Geographic-precision: the sentence opens with the western/northwestern reservation-edge canopy, then attributes its leaf-and-branch drain-clogging specifically to 'Village and Springfield Avenue roofs.' Maplewood Village and the Springfield Avenue corridor are the township's commercial core, not on the wooded western reservation edge (the reservation-edge canopy loads the Wyoming section per the brief). Defensible because the brief frames mature street-tree canopy as township-wide and 'the defining Maplewood roof stressor,' but the sentence over-couples the reservation-edge specifically to the Village/Springfield roofs.
findings.evidence: "**Reservation-edge tree canopy** along Maplewood's wooded western and northwestern edge, where the South Mountain Reservation reaches into the township, drops leaf load and broken branches that clog internal drains and back water onto Village and Springfield Avenue roofs."
findings.fix: before: '...drops leaf load and broken branches that clog internal drains and back water onto Village and Springfield Avenue roofs.' → after: '...and Maplewood's tree-lined streets drop leaf load and broken branches that clog internal drains and back water onto Village and Springfield Avenue roofs.' (attribute the Village/Springfield drain-clogging to the township-wide street-tree canopy rather than to the western reservation edge specifically; keep the reservation-edge angle for the Wyoming-section commercial/mixed-use roofs as commercial-roof-replacement.ts challenge[3] already does).

findings.issue: Minor over-attribution: the ponding-defect definition ('ponding held more than 48 hours counts as a defect') and the minimum-slope rule ('at least one-quarter inch per foot of slope to drain') are NRCA/ARMA facts (per facts-causes-signs.md and facts-components-specialty.md; the Orange gold exemplar attributes them to 'NRCA and ARMA'). They are credited here to 'the RCMA and NRCA' — NRCA correctly owns both, but appending the RCMA to these two specific clauses is imprecise. The same sentence does carry legitimately RCMA-sourced content (acrylic re-emulsify / ponded-warranty point), so this is borderline, not a hard error.
findings.evidence: 'A low-slope roof needs at least one-quarter inch per foot of slope to drain, and ponding held more than 48 hours counts as a defect, per the RCMA and NRCA...'
findings.fix: Tighten the attribution on the slope/ponding clause to NRCA/ARMA. Before: '...needs at least one-quarter inch per foot of slope to drain, and ponding held more than 48 hours counts as a defect, per the RCMA and NRCA...' -> after: '...needs at least one-quarter inch per foot of slope to drain, and ponding held more than 48 hours counts as a defect, per the NRCA and ARMA...' (keep RCMA only where it backs the acrylic re-emulsify / ponded-warranty point).

findings.issue: The 1:150 net-free attic-ventilation ratio (1 sq ft per 150 sq ft of attic floor) is attributed to 'the NRCA and ARMA standard,' but per the fact packs (facts-components-specialty.md) the 1:150 minimum is the IRC R806.2 CODE provision, not an NRCA/ARMA standard. The freshest same-batch sibling — South Orange (roof-vent-installation-repair, soffit-installation-repair, custom-roof-design-consultation, roof-ice-dam-prevention) — correctly pins the 1:150 ratio to 'IRC R806.2 and ARMA,' so the correct attribution is established within this batch. (Note: ~57 older committed combos carry the same 'NRCA and ARMA' mis-pin, so this is a pre-existing site-wide pattern; flagged low because the freshest sibling does it correctly.)
findings.evidence: challenges[3]: 'because the NRCA and ARMA specify 1 square foot of net-free vent area per 150 square feet of attic floor' — process[0]: 'sizes ventilation against the NRCA and ARMA standard of 1 square foot of net-free vent area per 150 square feet of attic floor'
findings.fix: Change 'the NRCA and ARMA specify 1 square foot of net-free vent area per 150 square feet of attic floor' → 'the IRC R806.2 minimum is 1 square foot of net-free vent area per 150 square feet of attic floor, per IRC R806.2 and ARMA' (and keep the separate NRCA cite for the qualitative 'reduces heat and moisture stress' point), matching the committed South Orange siblings.

findings.issue: Same 1:150-ventilation mis-pin as the asphalt combo: the 1 sq ft per 150 sq ft net-free area ratio is attributed to 'the NRCA and ARMA standard,' but it is the IRC R806.2 code minimum (per facts-components-specialty.md). findings.fix: Change 'the NRCA and ARMA standard of 1 square foot of net-free vent area per 150 square feet of attic floor' → 'the IRC R806.2 minimum of 1 square foot of net-free vent area per 150 square feet of attic floor, per IRC R806.2 and ARMA' to match the committed South Orange siblings and the fact pack.

findings.issue: Orphaned InterNACHI attribution. The sentence cites 'per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart and the NRCA and ARMA' for a clause that contains NO lifespan/life-expectancy figure — only a membrane seam-failure-mode claim (EPDM/TPO fail at the seams) and the ponding>48hr=defect rule. InterNACHI is a lifespan-only chart; the ponding-defect and ¼-in-slope facts belong to NRCA/ARMA, and the seam-failure-mode is trade guidance, not the InterNACHI chart. The committed Nutley sibling cites InterNACHI ONLY for the seam-failure mode and does not bundle the ponding rule under it; here the chart is dragged in without any figure it actually backs.
findings.evidence: '...where EPDM fails most often at the seams and TPO at the welded seams, and ponding water held more than 48 hours counts as a defect, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart and the NRCA and ARMA.'
findings.fix: Drop the orphaned InterNACHI cite: change 'per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart and the NRCA and ARMA' → 'per the NRCA and ARMA' (the ponding>48hr defect is the NRCA/ARMA fact; the EPDM/TPO seam-failure mode is trade guidance and needs no InterNACHI lifespan attribution since no lifespan figure appears in this sentence).

findings.issue: The 'Does a silicone coating lower cooling costs' FAQ offers the EPA 11-27% peak-cooling figure as the only quantified energy figure on a page entirely about COMMERCIAL/institutional low-slope roofs (Village center, SOPAC, Seton Hall).
